etymologies.etymologyHTML: Uncertain. The verb was attested in 1892, noun in 1918 and interjection in 1942. Apparently related to Scots soom (“to buzz, hum”), dialectal English and Scots soom, swoom, sweem (“to spin or twirl at high speed”). Compare also dialectal English sweem (“to swoon, become dizzy or faint”).

definitions.definition: A humming noise from something moving very fast.
An augmentation of a view, by varying the focal length of a lens, or digitally.
To move fast with a humming noise.

quote.citation: 1957, Jack Kerouac, On the Road, Viking Press, →OCLC:
quote.text: […]  and it was strange sitting in their brand-new comfortable car and hearing them talk of exams as we zoomed smoothly into town.

definitions.definition: (photography) To change the focal length of a zoom lens.
To manipulate a display so as to magnify or shrink it.
(transitive) To check someone out; to investigate someone that one is interested in.

quote.citation: 1990 December 16, Chris Nealon, quoting Al Cunningham, “Essence Magazine Agrees To Run Gay Advertisement”, in Gay Community News, volume 18, number 22, page 13:
quote.text: "It boggles my mind what kind of mentality is at work there." He pointed to two recent issues of the magazine that featured cover stories were about Whitney Houston and Luther Vandross, two pop music icons whose sexual orientations have been widely speculated on in Black lesbian and gay communities. "It makes you wonder if it's an insult to the intelligence of Essence’s lesbian and gay leadership," Cunningham said. "Who's really zooming whom here?"

quote.citation: 1918, Annie Vivanti Chartres, The Outrage, page 196:
quote.text: Makowsky was playing the Bassgeige. Zoom... zoom-zoom.... The rest of the orchestra would join in presently.

quote.citation: 1939, Henry Miller, Tropic of Capricorn, Grove Press, published 1962, page 244:
quote.text: I would dance a few light fantastic steps to show which way the wind lay, and zoom! Like a breeze I was on the piano stool and doing a velocity exercise.

definitions.definition: Suggesting a sudden change, especially an improvement or an increase

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Genericization of the trademark Zoom, a video teleconferencing software.

definitions.definition: To participate in a video teleconferencing call.

quote.citation: 2022 September 27, Barclay Bram, “My Therapist, the Robot”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Then, later that day, I logged onto a zoom call and my mother and I set up our yoga mats in the living room, as we had been doing a couple of times a week during the pandemic.
